meta.title: About Home Gasifier — One Person, Lots of Research
meta.description: Home Gasifier is a one-person research site about wood gasification. I haven't built one yet — but I'm working toward it, and I want to share what I've learned along the way.

hero.title: One Person, Genuinely Curious
hero.subtitle: I'm not an expert. I haven't built a gasifier yet. But I've done a lot of research, and I want to share it in a way that's actually useful — and honest.

body.text: I got interested in wood gasification a while back and started digging into it. What I found was a lot of scattered forum posts, old PDFs, and YouTube videos — some great, some outdated, some just wrong. I wanted one place where I could organize what I was learning.

I genuinely want to help people. If you're curious about gasification — whether you're thinking about building one, just want to understand the technology, or are trying to figure out if it's even worth your time — I hope this site saves you some of the digging I had to do.

I haven't built a gasifier yet. That's important to say upfront. Everything here comes from research — manuals, academic papers, community forums, and the experiences of people who have actually built and run these systems. I'm not writing from personal hands-on experience, and I don't want to pretend otherwise.

principles.title: Honest about what I know
principles.body: I try to be clear about the difference between what the research says and what I've personally verified. If I'm not sure about something, I say so. I'd rather flag uncertainty than sound more confident than I am.

principles.title: Safety is not optional
principles.body: Carbon monoxide is genuinely dangerous. I take the safety information seriously because the consequences of getting it wrong are serious. I cover every hazard I've found in the research, and I don't downplay them.

principles.title: Show where the information comes from
principles.body: I try to link to primary sources — the FEMA manual, NREL research, FAO documents — so you can check my work. If a claim comes from a forum post or a builder's experience, I try to say that too.

principles.title: Beginner-friendly, no talking down
principles.body: I explain terms when I use them and try to write for someone who is new to this — because not long ago, that was me. I also link to deeper resources for people who want to go further.

body.text: The guides here draw on primary sources: the FEMA emergency gasifier manual, Imbert gasifier design literature, academic research on biomass thermochemistry, and the collective knowledge of the gasification community built up over decades.
I try to cross-reference claims as best I can against engineering standards where they exist, and I flag areas of genuine uncertainty rather than papering over them with confident-sounding prose.

This site is a work in progress. I update it as I learn more, and I'm planning to document my own build when I get there. If you spot something that's wrong or outdated, I genuinely want to know — there's a contact link in the footer.

disclaimer.heading: A Note on Accuracy & Liability
disclaimer.body: The information on this site is provided for educational purposes by one person doing their best to research and organize it accurately. Gasification involves real hazards — carbon monoxide, fire, pressure, and chemical byproducts. Always verify local regulations before building, consult qualified professionals for structural or electrical work, and never operate a gasifier without proper safety equipment and ventilation. I am not a licensed engineer, and nothing here should be taken as professional advice. Use this information as a starting point for your own research, not as a final authority.

cta.heading: Start Exploring
cta.body: Whether you're just curious or seriously planning a build, the guides are here. We're both learning.
